## Standards

### Hard documented-contract violation — `src/reviewer-dispatch.ts:139–141, 310–318, 515–530`

`README.md:137` states: **“Infrastructure failures instead abort the action and exit nonzero.”** However, unexpected preflight infrastructure failures are converted into ordinary correctable proposal rejections:

> `throw new ReviewerPreflightError("preflight-infrastructure");`
> `return reject(identity, error);`

Consequently, failures such as Git process/I/O errors from `reader.resolve`, `range`, `material`, or `snapshot`, and malformed canonical-Skill section extraction, return a successful `Agent` tool result with `status: "rejected"` rather than invoking the fatal infrastructure path. The parent may retry even though changing the proposal cannot repair the underlying infrastructure or Skill snapshot. Preserve bounded diagnostics in evidence if required, but propagate this class through `failInfrastructure` so the action aborts nonzero as documented.

No baseline smell is reported: the otherwise broad ownership in `reviewer-dispatch.ts` is explicitly endorsed by repository authority as the sole capability/compiler/transition owner, overriding the Divergent Change heuristic.

Review facts concern pinned target `562bb9e74f04b0969c2eb774b224ea02d61d1d36`. The diff capture was tool scratch outside the clone; no probe or reviewed-target files were changed.

## Spec

- **[P2] Full commit IDs fail in SHA-256 Git repositories** — `src/reviewer-pinned-git.ts:62-72` recognizes full IDs only with `/^[0-9a-f]{40}$/`; a valid 64-character SHA-256 commit falls through to symbolic lookup and becomes `base-invalid`. This contradicts: “resolve the declared base commit only within the immutable pin.” The contract defines `revision: string`, not SHA-1-only revisions. Accept object IDs according to the repository’s object format or resolve them safely against the pinned reachable set.

- **[P2] Required packaged no-Spec lifecycle coverage is missing** — `test/reviewer-package-lifecycle.test.ts` contains only the established-Spec two-leg installed-package lifecycle. No packaged test exercises a Standards-only `not-established` proposal through dispatch, runner, audit, and receipt. The Plan explicitly requires: “one rejection-then-correction and both accepted cardinalities belong to `test/reviewer-package-lifecycle.test.ts`.” Unit tests cover the one-leg shape, but not the shipped extension/package boundary, so this Apply obligation is only partial.

No scope creep identified. The exact permitted diff command was run; broader test/typecheck commands were not authorized.

Summary: Standards — 1 finding; worst: infrastructure failures are misclassified as correctable rejections. Spec — 2 findings; worst: tied P2 issues in SHA-256 base resolution and missing packaged no-Spec lifecycle coverage.
